statement: Fix a finite data order m ≥ 10, a finite entry order r, a loss η > 0, and 0 < ν0 < 1. After fixing all the finite derivative orders needed below, one can choose ζ > 0 and then the finite formal accuracy orders in Proposition 4.6 so that the following hold for all sufficiently large parameters T in the packet sequence. There are smooth positive complete vacuum data d± T ∈ D on the whole bridge, with pm(d± T − d) −→ 0. (5.2) 27 In particular d± T ∈ U for large T. They agree exactly with d on the other end, the connecting region, and a protected region containing every fixed compact subset for large T. On the selected asymptotic end the protected ball is BT = {|z − z∗| < ρT }, z∗ = Ce(tT ), ρT = (1 − 2β)tT , (5.3) where β > 0 is fixed sufficiently small. The data have the weight-one metric and weight-two second- form symbol bounds at every order. Their full correction tails are retained; asymptotic coefficients are allowed to change. Ordinary exterior vacuum evolutions g± T , in exact wave-map gauge with the same target g, exist on the finite domains needed to reach ST , with fixed overlap margins and strict future-outflow artificial boundaries. Set H± T = \ g± T − g, F± T = H± T ∓ qT on the entry collar. Then Jr,T (F± T ) ≤ A2 T eηT , Jr,T (F+ T − F− T ) ≤ A3 T eηT . (5.4) The exact changes, packet, and errors vanish on the earlier needed entry interval v < (1 − ν0)T. In particular, r = 61 is permitted, with an arbitrarily small prescribed loss. The scaled linear deep residual can simultaneously be at most e−4κT through order 60, or at any other finite orders fixed in advance. The same statement holds for the separately prepared exchanged branch.
